message: Sleeping under 6 hours is linked to higher cortisol the next day, which can feel like being wired but tired.
Adenosine builds up while you are awake and clears during sleep. After a short night some is left over, which is linked to sleepiness and lower energy.
A full night of sleep supports the normal cortisol rhythm: high in the morning to wake you up, low at night.
Caffeine works by blocking adenosine, the molecule that makes you sleepy. More than 2 cups, especially late in the day, is linked to taking longer to fall asleep.
A lot of caffeine is linked to short-term rises in cortisol, which can feel like jitters or anxiety.
High anxiety goes with an active fight-or-flight response, where noradrenaline raises heart rate and alertness. Slow breathing and a short walk help the body settle.
GABA is the brain's calming signal. Sleep and exercise are linked to healthy GABA activity, so both are worth protecting on anxious days.
Daylight is linked to serotonin activity. You logged under 20 minutes outdoors; a short walk in daylight may help mood.
Skin makes vitamin D from sunlight. Little time outdoors, especially in winter, is linked to lower vitamin D.
Days are short where you are right now. Morning light helps set the body clock that times melatonin, so try to get outside early in the day.
30 minutes or more of movement today. Exercise is linked to dopamine release and to better motivation and mood.
Regular movement is linked to higher serotonin activity. Even 10 minutes of walking counts.
Low mood and low motivation are linked with dopamine and serotonin signalling, together with sleep, stress and life events. One low day is normal. If it lasts two weeks or more, talk to a GP.
Very low energy usually has everyday causes such as sleep. Thyroid hormones set the pace of your metabolism, so tiredness that lasts for weeks is worth mentioning to a GP.
Iron carries oxygen in your blood, and low iron is linked to tiredness. Skipping meals makes it harder to get enough.
Vitamin B12 supports blood and nerve cells, and low B12 is linked to tiredness and low mood. It comes from regular meals with animal products or fortified foods.
You took vitamin D today. Supplements are one way to keep levels up when there is little sun. Stay within the dose on the label.
